facts.text: Concepción was founded in 1550 by Pedro de Valdivia, originally named Concepción de María Purísima del Nuevo Extremo, and served as Chile's capital from 1565‑1573.
The city was repeatedly destroyed by earthquakes and tsunamis—most devastating in 1751—prompting its relocation to the Valle de la Mocha beside the Bío Bío River.
Concepción hosts Chile's first secular private university, the Universidad de Concepción, established in 1919.
The Teatro Biobío, a historic cultural venue, stands in Concepción’s historic district and has hosted generations of Chilean performers.
Known as Chile’s “capital of rock,” Concepción birthed bands like Los Tres and Los Bunkers, shaping the country’s music scene.
The city’s historic center lies in the Valle de la Mocha, the same valley where the original settlement was moved after the 1751 earthquake.
